title: Marguerite and the Ember Anew
premise: Dominic Sterling, royal food-taster and secret hedge-witch, has survived twelve years in the magic-outlawed city of Vellamare by being forgettable—until Marguerite, a feral child speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the Emberfolk, appears at his door pursued by the Crown's Ashen Wardens. The girl carries a living ember of the old faith, and whoever holds it can either rekindle magic across the realm or burn it out forever. Hunted through the city's underbelly, Dominic must choose between the belonging he built as an invisible servant and the identity he buried as the last Ember-sworn. In the end, he passes the ember to Marguerite—not as a burden but as a birthright—and surrenders himself to the Wardens so her light can spread beyond the walls, dying to his old name so a new one can be born.
about_author: B. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former line cook who claims to have learned storytelling from the regulars at a midnight diner. They write quiet fantasies about small people carrying enormous secrets.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We meet him mid-ritual: tasting the queen's soup, palming a protective charm into the broth, invisible among servants. Flashbacks hint at the night magic was outlawed and what he lost. Emotional beat: the ache of a man who has made smallness an art.

chapters.title: A Knock in Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A mud-caked child speaks words that predate kingdoms—words Dominic swore never to answer. He hides her as Ashen Wardens sweep the street. Emotional beat: terror and recognition; the past knocking literally at his door.

chapters.title: What the Ember Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, fragmented and sensory. She remembers fire, a burning village, a woman's last command: find the taster. The ember in her chest shows Dominic visions of the old faith. Emotional beat: memory as inheritance, grief shared without language.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Charms
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He weighs handing Marguerite over against the life he's built—his shop of harmless charms, his careful immunity, his place in the palace kitchens. An old contact offers escape for both if Dominic abandons the ember. Emotional beat: the seduction of staying safe.

chapters.title: The Warden's Question
chapters.summary: Warden Captain Ilse Vane's POV. Sharp, principled, she interrogates the kitchen staff and suspects the taster whose hands smell of herbs no apothecary sells. She offers Dominic a bargain: inform, and keep his name clean. Emotional beat: the hunter as mirror—another person shaped by loss.

chapters.title: Under the Salt Market
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Dominic and Marguerite flee through smuggler tunnels beneath the city, guided by a disgraced priestess who recognizes the ember and demands it for herself. Betrayal splits the group. Emotional beat: trust tested; belonging offered with strings attached.

chapters.title: Immunity
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Cornered, he poisons himself deliberately to buy time, surviving only because of twelve years of built tolerance—a lifetime of small sacrifices finally meaning something. Marguerite saves him with the ember's warmth. Emotional beat: his hidden discipline becomes visible courage.

chapters.title: The Queen's Table
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Captured and brought to the palace, she is fed by the queen herself—who tastes the ember's truth and reveals the monarchy outlawed magic not from fear but shame: the first king stole the flame. Emotional beat: history rewritten; enemies revealed as kin.

chapters.title: Ashes at the Gate
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, climax. He walks into the Wardens' stronghold openly, using his taster's access to reach Marguerite, while Ilse Vane must choose between duty and the truth she's uncovered. The ember flares; the city watches fire climb the palace spire. Emotional beat: invisibility abandoned at last.

chapters.title: Ember Anew
chapters.summary: Dual POV resolution. Dominic gives Marguerite the ember freely and takes the Wardens' chains so she can carry the flame beyond the walls to the scattered Emberfolk. Ilse lets him live in exile rather than execution. Final image: Marguerite on a far hillside, teaching other children the old words. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into legacy; a new name kindled.
